newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed, Boeing to battle for U.S. fighter jet.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Boeing to battle for U.S. fighter jet.

text.p: The Pentagon on Saturday picked industry teams led by Lockheed Martin Corp. and Boeing Co. to compete in a program to build 3,000 fighter jets in the 21st century that could mean over $170 billion to the eventual winner.
A third team headed by McDonnell Douglas Corp. was eliminated from the "joint strike fighter program" in the announcement by Defense Secretary William Perry at a Pentagon news conference.
The biggest weapons project of the early 21st century will provide a common "joint strike fighter" with some variations for the U.S. Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps and the British Navy.

Under the hotly-contested selection process, Lockheed and Boeing each will build a test model for a decision on the winner expected in the year 2001. The announcement was a major blow McDonnell Douglas, which was teamed with British Aerospace Plc and Northrop Grumman Corp. in the competition.

In addition to 3,000 jets now planned for the four services -- including 2,000 for the Air Force -- industry executives believe another 1,000 could be sold for export to U.S. allies if future budgets can keep the massive program alive.

Experts say the deal could one day be worth $170 billion or more for the final winner although aerospace firms say it could be several times that total if spare parts and other long-term items are included. Current plans are to build 2,036 for the Air Force, 300 for the Navy, 642 for the Marine Corps and 60 for the British Royal Navy.
